## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷakāliṅgajātaka* (Ja 301) is a story in the Pali Jātaka collection, translated into English under the title *King Kāliṅga*. According to its traditional framing, the Buddha delivered the tale while staying at the Jetavana monastery concerning the admission of four female ascetics to the monastic life, opening with the incipit phrase "Open the gate".

The Pali text and its commentary were edited in Latin script by V. Fausböll in the third volume of his edition of the Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1883].

  Within the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus identifies 6 text-reuse matches (encompassing 703 characters, with the longest corresponding to segment range §4.1–4.6) between the root text and the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
